copy.blurb:
Wednesday 24 June 2026 at 19:00 UTC. Switzerland and Canada on the card. On the Canada side, the engine's number sits +12.5pp clear of the market — a wide disagreement by the engine's standards this far out from kickoff.

Public Elo rates Canada 30 points higher than the other side (Switzerland 1830, Canada 1860). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Switzerland to win at 33%, the draw at 28%, and Canada to win at 39%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Switzerland to win at 48%, the draw at 27%, and Canada to win at 26%. Reading those three numbers as a probability distribution, the market's view is internally consistent. The disagreement with the model is concentrated on the Canada side — 26% on the market, 39% on the engine, a +12.5pp gap.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Canada the lower bound is 32%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +5.3pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. Calibration tracks the closing market on the bulk sample; selection — picking the single side where the gap is wide — is where the engine's edge has to come from. This verdict is a selection call on the Canada side.

The number above is the most recent read; it isn't frozen. With kickoff roughly 33 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. Injury news, the actual XI, and weather conditions at kickoff all feed back into the prior when they land. We republish on every refresh. The Desk surfaces edge; what to do with that surface is a reader's call.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Canada a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +12.5pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: A +12.5pp gap across model and market on the Canada side. Our Elo prior, after host and altitude adjustments, rates Canada at 39%; Polymarket sits at 26%.
copy.title: Switzerland v Canada · the model leans Canada
